claims.claim: Long-standing USGS standard procedure is to let sensors equilibrate to the temperature of the water being monitored before making field measurements, and sensors have equilibrated adequately when the variability among consecutive measurements does not exceed the criterion in table 6.0-1 for about five or more consecutive measurements.

Sensors have equilibrated adequately

does not exceed an established criterion.

claims.claim: For surface water, allow at least 60 seconds (or follow the manufacturer's guidelines) for sensors to equilibrate, take readings until the table 6.0-1 stabilization criteria are met, and record the median of the final three or more readings as the reported value for that measurement point.
claims.quote:
Surface water: Allow at least 60 seconds (or follow
the manufacturer’s guidelines) for sensors to equilibrate
with sample water.

claims.claim: For groundwater, begin recording after sensors have equilibrated with purge water, take readings until the table 6.0-1 stabilization criteria are met and the required number of well volumes have been purged, and record the median of the final five or more readings as the reported value for that site.

6.0–1 are met and the required number of well volumes
of groundwater have been purged. Record the median
of the final five or more readings

either use the median of the final five or
more measurements recorded, or apply knowledge of
the site and professional judgment to select the most
representative of the final readings

gaps: No calibration procedure for any metric. The chapter requires that sensors be calibrated and checked at the field site but defers every method to NFM chapters A6.1 through A6.8. Zero occurrences of buffer values or standard-solution concentrations anywhere in the document.

No stabilization criterion for ORP/Eh. Table 6.0-1 has no Eh row, and the chapter states explicitly that Eh is not a routine or direct field measurement. An operator asking what counts as a stable ORP reading cannot be answered from this document.
No stabilization criterion for alkalinity/ANC either, because the chapter classes it a field analysis requiring titration rather than a direct field measurement.
No ecological or health interpretation of any value. Zero occurrences of "healthy", "aquatic life", or "hypoxia". The chapter says how to obtain a defensible number and never what the number means.

The turbidity unit of measure is determined from a USGS Excel spreadsheet of turbidity-instrument models that is NOT part of this corpus. A question about which unit a given instrument reports is unanswerable from the corpus.

No guidance on unattended or continuous sonde deployment. Zero occurrences of "unattended", "fouling" or "biofouling". Continuous monitors are deferred to Wagner and others, which is not in this corpus.
No sample holding times or preservation guidance — zero occurrences of "holding time".
No instrument maintenance or replacement intervals; the chapter covers log-book record-keeping for instruments but not their service schedule.
No unit-conversion factors beyond volume (1 gallon = 3.785 liters) and the temperature C-to-F formula. No mg/L to percent-saturation conversion for DO, and no NTU/FNU conversion.
Surface-water procedure is far thinner than the groundwater procedure, which occupies most of section 3.2. An operator working a river has much less to go on here than one sampling a well.
